prompt: What is the SI unit of speed?

feedback.b: m/s² is the unit of acceleration.

hints: Speed = distance ÷ time. Divide the units too.
solution: Speed = distance (m) ÷ time (s), so the SI unit is **metres per second (m/s)**.

prompt: A sprinter runs 100 m in 20 s. What is her average speed?
hints: Speed = distance ÷ time.
solution: $v = \dfrac{d}{t} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5$ m/s

prompt: Match each quantity to its SI unit.
hints: Acceleration is a change in velocity (m/s) every second.
solution: Speed → m/s; acceleration → m/s²; distance → m; time → s.

prompt: Velocity is speed in a particular [[a]]. Acceleration is the rate of change of [[b]].
hints: "15 m/s north" is a velocity. What extra information does it have compared with a speed?
solution: Velocity is speed in a particular **direction**. Acceleration is the rate of change of **velocity**: how much the velocity changes each second.

options.text: Moving at a constant speed of 20 m/s

feedback.b: On a **speed**–time graph, a flat line means the speed isn't changing. The car is only stopped when the speed is 0.
feedback.c: Speeding up would be a line sloping upwards.
feedback.d: Slowing down would be a line sloping downwards.

hints: Read the axis labels: this is speed against time, not distance against time.
solution: The line is flat at 20 m/s, so the speed isn't changing: the car is moving at a **constant speed of 20 m/s**.

prompt: Which of these is an **instantaneous** speed?

options.text: A car's speedometer reads 80 km/h as it passes a sign
A family drives 240 km in 3 hours
A runner finishes a 5 km race in 25 minutes
A ferry takes 3 hours to cross 90 km of sea

feedback.b: Total distance ÷ total time gives an average speed for the whole trip.
feedback.c: This gives the runner's average speed over the whole race.
feedback.d: This gives the ferry's average speed for the crossing.

hints: Instantaneous means "at one instant" (one moment).
solution: The speedometer reading is the speed **at that moment**, so it is instantaneous. The others give average speeds (total distance ÷ total time).

prompt: How long does it take Sione to run 400 m at an average speed of 5 m/s?
hints: Rearrange speed = distance ÷ time to make time the subject.
solution: $t = \dfrac{d}{v} = \dfrac{400}{5} = 80$ s

prompt: What is the name of the quantity that tells you how quickly an object's velocity changes?
hints: Its unit is m/s².
solution: **Acceleration**: $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{t}$, measured in m/s².

options.text: A car speeding up as the traffic lights turn green
A cyclist braking to stop at a crossing
A car going round a roundabout at a steady 30 km/h
A train moving in a straight line at a steady 80 km/h
A car parked outside the dairy

hints: Acceleration is any change in **velocity**.
Velocity includes direction.
solution: Acceleration means the **velocity** changes. Speeding up (a) and slowing down (b) change the speed. Going round a roundabout (c) changes the **direction**, so the velocity changes even though the speed is steady. The steady train and the parked car have constant velocity, so they aren't accelerating.

prompt: What shape is the line on a **distance–time** graph for an object moving at a constant speed?

feedback.b: A horizontal line on a distance–time graph means the object is stopped.
feedback.c: A curve getting steeper means the object is speeding up.
feedback.d: A vertical line would mean moving a distance in no time at all, which is impossible.

hints: At constant speed, the same distance is covered every second.
solution: Constant speed means equal distances in equal times, which gives a **straight sloping line**. The steeper the line, the faster the speed.

prompt:
A bus travels from Hamilton to Auckland, a distance of about 125 km, in 2 hours. Its speedometer sometimes shows 0 km/h and sometimes 100 km/h.

Use this example to explain the difference between **average speed** and **instantaneous speed**. Include a calculation.
modelAnswer: Average speed is the total distance divided by the total time for the whole trip: 125 km ÷ 2 h = 62.5 km/h. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one particular moment, which is what the speedometer shows. It changes during the trip, from 0 km/h when the bus is stopped at lights to 100 km/h on the motorway. The average of 62.5 km/h doesn't mean the bus was ever going at exactly that speed.

rubric.criterion: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time for the whole journey
Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment (e.g. the speedometer reading), which varies during the trip

hints: Which speed uses the whole trip, and which is at a single moment?
solution: Average speed $= \dfrac{125 \text{ km}}{2 \text{ h}} = 62.5$ km/h for the whole trip. The speedometer shows the instantaneous speed, which goes up and down (0 to 100 km/h) during the journey.

prompt: A train travels 1.2 km in 1 minute 20 seconds. What is its average speed in **km/h**?
hints: It's easiest to work in m/s first: change 1.2 km to metres and 1 min 20 s to seconds.
Then multiply by 3.6 to change m/s into km/h.
solution: Distance = 1,200 m. Time = 60 + 20 = 80 s. Speed $= \dfrac{1200}{80} = 15$ m/s. In km/h: $15 \times 3.6 = 54$ km/h.

prompt: Car A goes from 0 to 100 km/h in 8 s. Car B goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 5 s. Which car has the greater acceleration?

options.text: Car B, about 4 m/s² compared with about 3.5 m/s²
Car A, because 100 is bigger than 20
Car A, about 12.5 m/s² compared with 4 m/s²

feedback.b: The speeds are in different units, so you can't compare 100 and 20 directly.
feedback.c: 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 uses km/h, not m/s. Change 100 km/h into m/s first.
feedback.d: Work out both accelerations in m/s² and compare them.

hints: Change Car A's speed into m/s first (divide by 3.6).
Then use $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{t}$ for each car.
solution: Car A: $100 \div 3.6 \approx 27.8$ m/s, so $a \approx \dfrac{27.8}{8} \approx 3.5$ m/s². Car B: $a = \dfrac{20}{5} = 4$ m/s². **Car B** has the greater acceleration.

prompt: Put these speeds in order from **slowest** to **fastest**.
hints: Change them all into m/s so you can compare them.
km/h ÷ 3.6 = m/s. For "400 m in 1 minute", divide by 60 s.
solution: In m/s: 1.5; $10 \div 3.6 \approx 2.8$; 4; $18 \div 3.6 = 5$; $400 \div 60 \approx 6.7$. So the order is 1.5 m/s → 10 km/h → 4 m/s → 18 km/h → 400 m in 1 minute.
